title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drainage Flow
description: A frequent installation error in residential drainage systems is using a standard sanitary tee in horizontal-to-horizontal drain transitions. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or horizontal branch connections entering a vertical stack. When installed horizontally, the short radius branch fails to direct waste smoothly, increasing the risk of clogs and hydraulic jumps. Instead, plumbing codes require long-sweep fittings, wyes, or combination wye and 1/8 bends for horizontal flow direction changes. Using the correct directional fitting maintains proper flow velocity and prevents solid waste build-up over time.

Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drainage Flow

A frequent installation error in residential drainage systems is using a standard sanitary tee in horizontal-to-horizontal drain transitions. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or horizontal branch connections entering a vertical stack. When installed horizontally, the short radius branch fails to direct waste smoothly, increasing the risk of clogs and hydraulic jumps. Instead, plumbing codes require long-sweep fittings, wyes, or combination wye and 1/8 bends for horizontal flow direction changes. Using the correct directional fitting maintains proper flow velocity and prevents solid waste build-up over time.
